name: Niacinamide
description: A water-soluble form of vitamin B3 that strengthens the skin barrier, regulates sebum and visibly evens tone.
benefits: Reduces visible pore size and oiliness
usage: 2-10% in a serum, morning and/or night, applied after cleansing on damp skin.
avoidMixingReason: High-dose pure L-ascorbic acid with high-dose niacinamide can cause temporary flushing; separate them morning and night.

name: Retinol
description: A vitamin A derivative that accelerates cell turnover and stimulates collagen, the most studied anti-ageing active.
usage: Night only. Start 0.1-0.3% twice weekly, build to nightly. Always pair with SPF 50 the next morning.
avoidMixingReason: Layering with strong acids or benzoyl peroxide multiplies irritation and can degrade the retinoid.

name: Salicylic Acid
description: An oil-soluble beta hydroxy acid that clears inside the pore lining, making it the first choice for congestion and blackheads.
usage: 0.5-2% leave-on 2-4 nights per week, or as a daily cleanser for oily skin.
avoidMixingReason: Stacked exfoliation strips the barrier; alternate nights instead.

name: Vitamin C
description: A potent daytime antioxidant that neutralises free radicals, brightens tone and supports collagen synthesis.
sideEffects: Oxidises to an orange tint when expired
usage: 10-20% each morning on clean skin, followed by moisturiser and SPF.
avoidMixingReason: pH conflicts reduce stability and increase irritation; use vitamin C in the morning, retinoids at night.

name: Azelaic Acid
description: A gentle dicarboxylic acid that targets redness, pigmentation and acne bacteria simultaneously.
usage: 10-20% once or twice daily after cleansing.

name: Ceramides
description: Lipids naturally present in the stratum corneum that seal moisture in and keep irritants out.
sideEffects: Rarely, heaviness on very oily skin
usage: In a moisturiser, morning and night, as the final hydrating step.

name: Hyaluronic Acid
description: A humectant that binds up to 1000x its weight in water, plumping the surface layers instantly.
sideEffects: Can feel tight in dry climates if not sealed with a moisturiser
usage: Apply to damp skin, then lock in with a moisturiser.

name: Benzoyl Peroxide
description: An oxygen-releasing antibacterial that reduces C. acnes populations inside the follicle.
usage: 2.5-5% as a short-contact wash or targeted leave-on at night.
avoidMixingReason: Oxidises retinoids and ascorbic acid, reducing both actives' efficacy.

name: Glycolic / Lactic Acid
description: Water-soluble acids that loosen the bonds between dead surface cells for smoother, brighter skin.
usage: 5-10% twice weekly at night. Always follow with SPF the next day.

name: Peptides
description: Short amino-acid chains that signal the skin to produce more structural proteins.
usage: Morning and night in a serum or moisturiser.
avoidMixingReason: Generally compatible; avoid layering directly with very low-pH acids.

name: Zinc PCA
description: A zinc salt that regulates sebum output and provides light antibacterial support.
usage: 1% in a serum, morning or night.

name: Broad Spectrum SPF
description: The single highest-impact step for preventing pigmentation, photoageing and post-inflammatory marks.
benefits: Essential alongside every exfoliant or retinoid
sideEffects: White cast with some mineral filters
usage: SPF 30-50 every morning, two fingers for face and neck, reapply every 2-3 hours outdoors.
avoidMixingReason: Apply as the final morning step.

name: Vitamin E
description: A lipid-soluble antioxidant that stabilises vitamin C and protects cell membranes.
sideEffects: Can feel occlusive on acne-prone skin
usage: 0.5-1% alongside vitamin C in the morning.

name: Ferulic Acid
description: A plant antioxidant used to stabilise and amplify vitamin C and E formulations.
